choices.text: Place the cancellable hold at Hospital Tower Hotel; include a call or message to reservations to verify whether the assigned queen room has an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge before finalizing, and note that the indoor lab access is why it remains the lead.
Place the cancellable hold at Uptown Suites because it already shows the in-room brewer and mini-fridge and still has a reasonable rideshare to the lab.
Place the cancellable hold at Downtown Residence because its in-room setup and full recovery amenities are confirmed, accepting the longer morning rideshare.
Place the cancellable hold at University Guesthouse as the lowest-rate close option, and add only a refrigerator-request note to the reservation.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Medium-hard because Uptown Suites cleanly satisfies the room-appliance details, while Hospital Tower is stronger on the current trip logistics and should not be rejected solely for an unconfirmed listing.
probes.gold_action: Hold Hospital Tower Hotel as the lead and verify the unclear in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge details rather than dropping it solely for the blank appliance line.
probes.label_rationale: Kara often wants in-room coffee and cold storage for early clinic or teaching trips, but she has also treated a late or non-guaranteed fridge as something to confirm or request rather than a reason to abandon an otherwise strong hotel. Hospital Tower also fits the queen-room, rating, commute, and recovery-amenity patterns, so the right move is to keep it as the lead while verifying the missing room details.
probes.query: Kara is holding off on final booking for a Sunday-Wednesday Cleveland pediatric seating lab until the hospital confirms badge access. The first two mornings start at 7:30, she will not rent a car, and all rates below are cancellable and within the sponsor cap. Hospital Tower Hotel is $218, 4.4-rated, attached to the lab building by an indoor walkway, with a queen room, fitness room, indoor pool, and hot tub; the room page lists standard furnishings but leaves the in-room beverage/appliance line blank while rooms are being refreshed. Uptown Suites is $214, 4.5-rated, an 8-11 minute rideshare, with a queen studio, in-room brewer and mini-fridge, breakfast, fitness room, and pool, with no hot tub listed. University Guesthouse is $209, 4.3-rated, a 6-9 minute rideshare or 18-minute walk, with a queen room, in-room brewer, refrigerator by request, and fitness room only. Downtown Residence is $216, 4.6-rated, a 14-18 minute rideshare, with a queen studio with in-room brewer and mini-fridge, fitness room, indoor pool, and hot tub. Which one-hold note should the planner send tonight?

choices.text: Keep Conference Tower Hotel as the lead and send reservations a specific room-setup verification request for an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge; do not switch solely because the website omits those room details.
Switch the lead to Garden District Suites because its queen studio already confirms the in-room brewer and mini-fridge, even though it is a short ride from the conference tower and lacks a hot tub.
Switch the lead to Warehouse Residence because the in-room setup is confirmed and the streetcar or rideshare is manageable, while noting the seasonal hot tub closure.
Switch the lead to Riverfront Boutique because it has the highest guest score and dinner access, with the refrigerator request written into the booking notes.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard because the suite option looks safer on the room details, but the stronger all-around conference fit makes the correct action a verification step rather than an immediate switch.
probes.gold_action: Keep Conference Tower Hotel first and verify or request the in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge rather than automatically moving to a farther confirmed-appliance hotel.
probes.label_rationale: The conference-tower option matches multiple recurring priorities: a good rating, queen room, pool, hot tub, fitness access, and the least friction for early conference events. The missing in-room coffee and refrigerator details still matter, but Kara's prior decisions support verifying or requesting them when the hotel otherwise fits the trip instead of treating the omission as an automatic dealbreaker.
probes.query: Kara has to update an unbooked hotel plan for a Thursday-Sunday pediatric neurodevelopment conference in New Orleans. Friday registration and Saturday's 8:00 skills lab are inside the conference tower; she is using rideshares only, and each option below is refundable with similar totals. Conference Tower Hotel is 4.4-rated, in the same building as registration and the lab, with a queen room, fitness room, outdoor pool, and hot tub; its current room details mention a lobby café but do not specify a room coffee maker or refrigerator. Garden District Suites is 4.5-rated, an 8-10 minute rideshare, with a queen studio, in-room brewer and mini-fridge, breakfast and fitness room, and no hot tub listed. Warehouse Residence is 4.3-rated, a 10-12 minute rideshare or streetcar, with a queen studio, in-room brewer and mini-fridge, fitness room and pool, and a seasonal hot tub closed on the trip dates. Riverfront Boutique is 4.6-rated, a 7-9 minute rideshare, with a queen room, in-room brewer, refrigerator on request, fitness room only, and the best nearby dinner options. What should be the lead update?

choices.text: Keep Medical Center Block first, mark the mini-fridge as a specific request to confirm with reservations, and ask Kara before switching if the hotel later says it cannot provide one.
Move Five Points Suites first because it confirms both in-room items and keeps the drive manageable, despite losing the hot tub and immediate classroom access.
Move Homewood Southside first because it has the confirmed room setup plus pool, hot tub, and fitness, while noting the stricter cancellation deadline.
Use Airport Hampton as the budget fallback because it has the room appliances and easy airport return, while warning about the longer medical-center drive.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Medium-hard because Five Points Suites is a credible safer pick on in-room details, while Medical Center Block wins only if the soft room-appliance issue is handled as a confirm-and-ask item.
probes.gold_action: Rank Medical Center Block first and treat the mini-fridge issue as a confirmation/request item, not a reason by itself to discard the strongest medical-center fit.
probes.label_rationale: For this training, Medical Center Block best supports the early supply-cart pickup, tight parking situation, queen-room setup, good rating, and recovery amenities. Kara's pattern makes the fridge request important, but when the rest of the hotel strongly fits the trip, the better move is to confirm and escalate the issue to her if needed rather than automatically selecting a farther hotel.
probes.query: Kara is choosing a Monday-Thursday Birmingham hotel for a pediatric gait-and-casting training. The first morning has a 7:20 supply-cart pickup at the children's hospital, the classroom is in the medical center, and she will have a compact rental car, but parking at the training garage is tight. All hotels are refundable and acceptable to the host. Medical Center Block is $189, 4.3-rated, a 3-minute walk from the classroom, with a queen room, fitness room, indoor pool, and hot tub; reservations says in-room brewers are standard but mini-fridges are allocated by request and cannot be guaranteed until assignment. Five Points Suites is $184, 4.4-rated, a 7-10 minute drive, with a queen studio, in-room brewer and mini-fridge, breakfast, pool, and fitness room, but no hot tub. Homewood Southside is $192, 4.5-rated, a 9-13 minute drive, with a queen suite, in-room brewer and mini-fridge, fitness room, pool, and hot tub, with a slightly tighter cancellation deadline. Airport Hampton is $176, 4.2-rated, an 18-24 minute drive, with a queen room, in-room brewer and mini-fridge, breakfast, fitness room, and pool. Which recommendation should go first?
